# Tools & Data Sources {#sec-appendix-tools}

PhyloTrace does not implement the heavy bioinformatics itself; it drives
established, published tools and cites their results. This appendix lists them,
so that you can name them in a methods section, and lists the external services
the app contacts.

## The analysis toolchain

| Tool | What it does in PhyloTrace | Chapter |
|---|---|---|
| **pyMLST** [@pymlst] | cgMLST and classical MLST typing; downloading schemes | @sec-typing, @sec-schemes |
| **BLAT** | Aligning an assembly against the scheme's alleles | @sec-typing |
| **MAFFT** | Sequence alignment where typing needs it | @sec-typing |
| **abritamr** [@sherry2023abritamr] | Curating AMR results into drug classes | @sec-amr |
| **NCBI AMRFinderPlus** [@feldgarden2021amrfinderplus] | Detecting AMR, virulence and stress determinants | @sec-amr |

These are installed with PhyloTrace at **fixed versions**, deliberately: the app
reads their output precisely, so the versions are part of the installation rather
than something to update independently. The exact version used for any isolate is
recorded with that isolate (@sec-typing-provenance), which is what you should
quote in a methods section rather than "the latest".

## Reference data and external services

| Source | What PhyloTrace requests | Chapter |
|---|---|---|
| **cgMLST.org** [@cgmlstorg] | The cgMLST scheme for a species | @sec-schemes |
| **PubMLST** / **Institut Pasteur** [@pubmlst] | The matching classical 7-gene MLST scheme | @sec-typing |
| **NCBI AMRFinderPlus database** | The AMR/virulence/stress reference sequences | @sec-amr |
| **OpenStreetMap / Nominatim** | Coordinates for a place name | @sec-map |
| **Natural Earth** | Country outlines for the choropleth map | @sec-map |

::: {.callout-important title="No isolate data is sent to any of these"}
Every one of these requests either downloads public reference data or resolves a
place name. Your assemblies, allele profiles and metadata never leave your
machine (@sec-app-local).
:::

## Methods-section wording

A typical methods sentence built from the above:

> Assemblies were typed by core-genome MLST against the *[species]* scheme from
> cgMLST.org using PhyloTrace *[version]*, which drives pyMLST *[version]* with
> BLAT for allele calling. Classical seven-gene sequence types were resolved
> against *[PubMLST / Institut Pasteur]*. Antimicrobial-resistance, virulence and
> stress determinants were identified with NCBI AMRFinderPlus *[version]*
> (database *[version]*) via abritamr *[version]*. Pairwise allelic distances
> were computed as Hamming distances between allele profiles with *[NA-handling
> policy]*, and minimum spanning trees were constructed from the resulting
> distance matrix.

Every bracketed value is recorded in your database and can be read off an
isolate's provenance record (@sec-typing-provenance).
